Luke Humphries ‘feeling much better’ after trapped nerve threatened Players Championship Finals hopes
Luke Humphries is confident he can get back to performing at his best at this week's Players Championship Finals after injuries have blighted his form; Humphries revealed he had been suffering from a trapped nerve in his shoulder in the build-up to the Grand Slam of Darts
Thursday 26 November 2026 18:16, UK
Luke Humphries is feeling "much better" ahead of this week's Players Championship Finals, revealing he has beeing suffering with a trapped nerve in his shoulder during his shock last-16 exit against Tom Sykes at last week's Grand Slam of Darts.
Humphries was seen wincing in pain during the match and later cast doubt on social media about whether he would feature in this week's tournament, explaining he had gone through a tough 48 hours before facing Sykes.
On Thursday, the 31-year-old revealed that he had been managing the injury for some time.

"Unfortunately, [my season] has taken a little stride back last week with the trapped nerve in my back; it's a recurring thing that's happened quite a few times now," Humphries told Sky Sports.
"I'm going to have to get it sorted and find ways to stop it from coming back, because when you're playing in major tournaments, the last thing you need is that kind of thing lingering.
"It's much better now; after a week off, it's much more repaired. Hopefully, going into the Players Championship Finals this weekend, I can play injury-free, and hopefully I go on to win."
Humphries expressed his frustration at how injuries and illness have hampered the back end of his season.
The Englishman had hoped to build on his World Grand Prix victory and win his first European Championship, but was forced to withdraw from October's tournament due to illness.
"It's quite unfortunate because I've been playing really good," Humphries said.
"The European Championships I had to [withdraw] because I wasn't well. So, it's been a little bit of a disappointment for me in the past couple of majors, after I won the Grand Prix.
"I was looking to cash in on that and do really well."
Humphries is out to win his third Players Championship Finals this week and will play Darryl Pilgrim in the opening round on Friday night in Minehead.
Humphries adds he's been working hard alongside his physio to reduce the effects of the injury and if he can do that, he backs himself to get back to playing his best.
"It's just something you can't stop. There's nothing you can do about it. It's not like I'm doing anything to make it happen," he said.
"It's just something that recurs, and something that me and my physio, John, we're working through and are trying to build a bit of strength in it and stop it recurring.
"If I can stay injury-free, everyone knows how well I play and the consistency I [have] showed this year.
"Hopefully an injury-free back of the year."
